references.text: Parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus tells the same parable about the unclean spirit that returns with seven other spirits worse than itself, and the final state becomes worse than the first.

Peter writes that if anyone has escaped the world's impurity by knowing the Lord Jesus Christ but is again caught and overcome, then the last state has become worse than the first – the same principle of falling away.

The book of Hebrews warns about those who have been enlightened and tasted the heavenly gift but fall away – their final condition is worse, in line with the principle that the last things become worse than the first.

The book of Hebrews warns that if we sin deliberately after receiving knowledge of the truth, only a terrible judgment remains – this illustrates the same principle of a worsened state after falling away.
The preceding verses in the same pericope describe the unclean spirit leaving a person, wandering through dry places, and returning to find the house swept and adorned – the context for verse 26.
Parallel passage in Matthew describing the unclean spirit's journey and return to the empty, swept house, which forms the basis for seven worse spirits moving in.
